summary:
The Pitcairn Islands stand under the United Kingdom's framework: defence and external affairs are reserved to the United Kingdom, and United Kingdom domestic measures such as the Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex-services code do not apply here of their own force. Local law governs, and those measures could reach Pitcairn only by Order in Council. Military service is likewise a United Kingdom responsibility rather than a local one.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2001.

The Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, and that guarantee has been in force since 2010.

Same-sex marriage has been legal since 14 May 2015. The Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 defines marriage as the union of two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity, and it recognises civil partnerships performed outside Pitcairn. The Island Council approved the ordinance unanimously on 1 April 2015; Governor Jonathan Sinclair signed it on 5 May 2015 and it was published on 13 May 2015, taking effect on 14 May.

Adoption has been legal since 2015 and is open to married, unmarried and single people.
tangentialFactors:
Because defence and external affairs are reserved to the United Kingdom, matters touching armed service, and any extension of United Kingdom equality or single-sex-services measures to the territory, are decided outside Pitcairn and would arrive only through an Order in Council.

The territory is commonly indexed within United Kingdom LGBT-rights timelines, which is a classification choice by the source publishers rather than a statement about the force of United Kingdom law locally.
localsOnly:
The resident population is roughly 50 people, and none of them is known to be in a same-sex relationship, so the practical reach of the 2015 marriage and partnership rules among residents is untested in daily life.

Local residents may rely on the Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 discrimination guarantee and on the Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015, including recognition of civil partnerships formed outside the territory; adoption is available to single as well as partnered residents.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory contains nothing on trans-specific questions: legal gender recognition, identity documents and markers, entry or arrival screening, access to healthcare, or facilities rules are unresolved here and are not sourced. Hate-crime provisions covering gender identity are likewise not addressed in the available material.

Substantive content is drawn from aggregator pages and a full republication of a Wikipedia article; the underlying ordinance text and the Constitution Order itself were not separately consulted, so the enactment dates and the council vote as reported should be treated as reported rather than independently verified.
